summary_of_core_decisions: The essay argues that Kant's ethics, properly understood, permits revolution when it is motivated by duty to justice rather than inclination toward happiness, and when the government is evil. It reconciles Kant's apparent condemnation of revolution with his sympathy for the French Revolution by emphasizing the role of the good will and the distinction between ideal and practical realms.
